svg.title: The OSI model with the device, data unit, and typical attacks at each layer
svg.desc: Seven layers built from the bottom up. Layer 1 Physical carries bits over cables, radio, and fiber, attacked by wiretapping and jamming. Layer 2 Data Link moves frames by MAC address through switches, attacked by ARP spoofing and MAC flooding. Layer 3 Network routes packets by IP address through routers, attacked by IP spoofing and BGP hijacking. Layer 4 Transport carries segments over TCP and UDP ports, filtered by firewalls, attacked by SYN floods and port scans. Layers 5 to 7 carry data for sessions, TLS, and applications such as HTTP, attacked by session hijacking, SSL stripping, injection, and phishing.
svg.text: The OSI model with the device, data unit, and typical attacks at each layer
Encapsulation runs top to bottom on the sender and bottom to top on the receiver; a defender asks what can go wrong at each layer.
